title: Require declaration verification before a File Candidate succeeds
objective: Turn the successful one-file declaration experiments into one production admission rule: the OpenCode Adapter may return a File Candidate only after deterministic SCORE code checks its exact final bytes against every relevant owned declaration frozen in that File Job.
requirements: SCORE derives one deterministic declaration verdict from the frozen File Job and the exact final candidate bytes, checks every owned declaration together in approved order, and returns not applicable when the approved owned-declaration list is empty.

The OpenCode Adapter cannot return a successful File Candidate when declaration input binding fails, the candidate digest does not match the checked bytes, or any relevant declaration finding remains; this final check is independent of optional Agent feedback and repair hooks.

A failed declaration check retains only bounded sanitized typed findings, the binding digest when binding completed, the exact candidate digest, and the verdict digest when a verdict was produced through existing Failure Evidence and Runner storage.

Human-readable failure output names each retained declaration finding and available digest without exposing candidate source, prompt content, parser diagnostics, local paths, credentials, or other raw runtime data.

Regression coverage proves valid and invalid multi-declaration candidates, exact frozen-input binding, post-feedback byte changes, deterministic repeated results, empty declaration lists, durable evidence recovery, sanitization, and human-readable failure output.

Verification remains bounded to one assigned file and runs entirely in memory after ordinary candidate capture; it performs no repository write, project command, environment loading, dependency installation, TypeScript assignability check, build, test, lint, runtime, or multi-file complete-set verification.

Production code does not import prototype modules or copy the large declaration-contract experiment wholesale; it extracts only the accepted one-file owned-declaration behavior needed at this gate and leaves prototype feedback and automatic repair policy unchanged.

owns.name: FileCandidateDeclarationVerdict
owns.declaration: export type FileCandidateDeclarationVerdict = { readonly status: "not_applicable"; readonly findings: readonly []; readonly bindingDigest: null; readonly candidateDigest: string; readonly verdictDigest: null; } | { readonly status: "valid"; readonly findings: readonly []; readonly bindingDigest: string; readonly candidateDigest: string; readonly verdictDigest: string; } | { readonly status: "invalid"; readonly findings: readonly [CandidateDeclarationFinding, ...CandidateDeclarationFinding[]]; readonly bindingDigest: string | null; readonly candidateDigest: string; readonly verdictDigest: string | null; };
owns.description: The deterministic one-file gate result. A valid result is bound to the approved inputs and exact candidate bytes; an invalid result always has at least one typed finding.

owns.name: verifyFileCandidateDeclarations
owns.declaration: export function verifyFileCandidateDeclarations(input: { readonly targetPath: string; readonly operation: "create" | "replace"; readonly agentInputJson: string; readonly packageDigest: string; readonly candidateSource: string; readonly targetOutputDigest: string; }): FileCandidateDeclarationVerdict;
owns.description: Checks every relevant declaration frozen for one File Job against the exact captured candidate and returns a deterministic verdict without reading or changing the repository.

context.purpose: Feasibility evidence for strict target, baseline, declaration-list, and digest binding. Reuse its accepted meanings, not its approved-export reconstruction or prototype API.
Feasibility evidence for the exact one-file finding projection and candidate/verdict digests. Do not import this prototype.

Reference the accepted OXC comparison behavior and stable finding order only where needed for owned declarations and their local supporting declarations. Do not copy its repository-scale evidence compiler wholesale.
Use the existing canonical JSON and SHA-256 helpers for byte and verdict binding.
Keep the production gate inside the accepted assurance boundary and explicit non-claims.

constraints: Import `type CandidateDeclarationFinding` from `./domain.js`. Do not import any module under `src/prototypes/`.

Treat `agentInputJson` and `packageDigest` as frozen fields of the already integrity-checked ClaimedJob. Parse JSON with the repository's duplicate-key-safe parser, require target path and operation to match the function input, obtain exact create absence or replace baseline bytes from the approved target-state data, and require each non-empty owned declaration entry to have a string name and declaration with no duplicate names.

If the frozen Agent Input has a valid empty owned-declaration list, return `not_applicable`. Malformed, mismatched, ambiguous, or unsupported relevant declaration input returns `invalid`; never silently drop one entry from a non-empty owned list.

Compute `candidateDigest` directly from the UTF-8 `candidateSource` and return an invalid candidate-digest finding if it differs from `targetOutputDigest`. Never authorize bytes using an earlier Agent-side or repair-hook verdict.

For the accepted one-file subset, compare every owned exported declaration and the local supporting declarations needed by its shape. Preserve approved order for checks and stable source order for findings. Report missing, unexpected, rerouted, incomplete, unsupported, syntax-invalid, or structurally mismatched relevant declarations with stable uppercase codes, declaration name or null, and generic source-free messages.

Bind the normalized target, operation, base digest, package digest, and complete ordered declaration list into `bindingDigest`. Bind the binding digest, candidate digest, normalized contracts, and ordered findings into `verdictDigest`. Repeated byte-identical inputs must return byte-identical objects and digests.

Return fresh plain data only. Do not return AST nodes, parser-owned mutable objects, raw parser diagnostics, source excerpts, prompts, local paths beyond the approved project-relative target, or thrown parser errors.

Use the pinned `oxc-parser` directly in memory. Do not call `inspect-module`, read `tsconfig.json`, resolve packages, inspect imports outside the assigned file, run commands, or claim TypeScript semantic assignability.

constraints: Import `type CandidateDeclarationFinding` and `type CandidateDeclarationFailureEvidence` from `./domain.js`.

Accept only digest strings matching `sha256:` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Store candidateDigest only when valid; bindingDigest and verdictDigest become null when absent or invalid.

Keep at most 32 findings. Keep only uppercase underscore-separated finding codes up to 96 characters, declaration names up to 120 terminal-safe characters or null, and messages passed through existing diagnostic redaction and terminal-safe length limits. Never preserve additional input properties.

Extend `sanitizeFailureEvidence` without changing its existing signature or any existing field behavior. Omit `declarationVerification` when no safe evidence object with a valid candidate digest remains.
Do not log or persist the rejected source, Agent Input, prompt text, raw diagnostic, AST, environment value, absolute path, or credential while sanitizing.

constraints: Import `verifyFileCandidateDeclarations` and `type FileCandidateDeclarationVerdict` from `./candidate-declaration-gate.js`, and import `type CandidateDeclarationFailureEvidence` from `./domain.js`.

Call `verifyFileCandidateDeclarations({ targetPath: job.targetPath, operation: job.operation, agentInputJson: job.agentInputJson, packageDigest: job.packageDigest, candidateSource: candidate.content, targetOutputDigest: candidate.targetOutputDigest })` immediately after `readCandidate` returns exact contained bytes and before any successful AdapterCandidate return. Delete operations remain rejected by the existing adapter before this call.

Continue on `not_applicable` or `valid`. On `invalid`, throw one typed internal candidate-declaration failure that carries only the returned findings and digests plus existing target-output evidence; map it to `failureEvidence.category === "candidate integrity"` with optional `declarationVerification` after sanitization.

The human-safe generic reason may summarize the first finding code and declaration name, but it must not interpolate source, Agent Input, raw parser errors, prompts, absolute paths, or credentials. Structured findings remain the authoritative detail.

Keep the existing `prototypeAgentPreflight`, `prototypeAutomaticRepair`, and `prototypeFinalCandidateCheck` behavior available for experiments, but none may bypass, replace, or supply the production verdict. If a prototype repair changes bytes, the production check evaluates only the newly captured final bytes.

Do not change gateway process execution, workspace containment, Agent prompting, repair count, paid invocation policy, Runner success timing, retry eligibility, repository application, or any non-OpenCode adapter.
